channel.title: Forgejo on ProHomeLab – everything about homelab and self-hosting
channel.description: Recent content in Forgejo on ProHomeLab – everything about homelab and self-hosting

item.title: GitLab, Gitea, and Forgejo. A Comparison for Grown-Ups - What Actually Fits Your Homelab
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: Comparing GitLab CE, Gitea, and Forgejo on licensing, hardware requirements, project governance, and CI/CD - and explaining why the advice to “just use GitLab, everything else is for people who don’t know better” has nothing to do with actual engineering arguments.

item.title: When Simpler Doesn't Mean Better: Going Back to Two Forgejo Repositories
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: Why self-hosted GitHub Actions on a single repository (article 3) turned out not to be the choice worth keeping - and how I reverted back to the proven two-repository Forgejo setup, walking through an honest comparison of both options along the way.

item.title: Removing the Middleman: Migrating from My Own Forgejo Runner to Self-Hosted GitHub Actions
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: How I moved the build and deploy of ProHomelab from a homemade Forgejo runner to a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner on my own LXC, merged content and site into a single repository - and what didn’t go according to plan.

item.title: Moving from Shared Hosting to GitHub Pages: Migrating a Hugo Site without Breaking a Single Link or Dropping Out of Google and Yandex Indexes
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: Migrating ProHomeLab from its old shared host to GitHub Pages on top of an already configured Obsidian → Forgejo → Hugo pipeline, while preserving all URLs and search engine rankings.

item.title: ProHomelab: Automating Article Publishing via Forgejo
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: Fully automating ProHomeLab publishing: I write an article in Obsidian, the changes automatically land in Forgejo, Forgejo Actions triggers a Hugo build on a Blowfish LXC, and the finished site gets uploaded with no manual steps at all.

item.title: GitOps for Homelab: Deploying Forgejo and Komodo From Scratch
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: A detailed GitOps tutorial for beginners: deploying Forgejo as your own git server, Komodo to manage Docker stacks, and configuring auto-deploy on push, with every configuration parameter explained along the way.

item.title: Forgejo + Komodo: Turning Docker Compose into GitOps
item.author: pavel@prohomelab.com (Stilicho2011)
item.description: Step by step, we build a GitOps setup for Docker Compose: Forgejo stores the configuration in Git, Komodo watches for changes and automatically updates the stacks on multiple servers.
